parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish آزیق (azık), from Proto-Common Turkic *āzuk, itself from Sogdian 𐼰𐼹𐼴𐼸 (ʾδwk /⁠āδūk⁠/, “grain, crop”). Cognate with Salar asuq, azuq, Turkmen azyk, Kazakh азық (azıq, “food”).

Inherited from Ottoman Turkish قادین (kadın), from Proto-Common Turkic *xātun (“queen, lady”), most likely from Sogdian [script needed] (γwtʾynh /⁠xwatēn, xutēn⁠/, “queen”). Akin to Old Turkic 𐰴𐱃𐰆𐰣 (qatun, “queen”), Karakhanid قاتُونْ (qātūn, “noble woman”), Yakut хотун (xotun).
From Ottoman Turkish قانجیق (kancık), from Proto-Common Turkic *kančïk (“bitch; female”), ultimately derived from Sogdian. Cognate with Kyrgyz канчык (kancık), Southern Altai канчык (kančïk).

From Ottoman Turkish قاطر (katır), from Proto-Common Turkic *katïr (“mule”), ultimately from Sogdian. Cognate with Old Turkic [script needed] (katır, “mule”), Kazakh қашыр (qašır), Kyrgyz качыр (kacır), Uzbek xachir, Azerbaijani qatır, Uyghur خېچىر (xëchir), etc. Also see Romanian catâr, Tajik хачир
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish صپا (sıpa), from Proto-Common Turkic *sïp (“colt of a donkey”), ultimately from Sogdian.

parole.significato: hell (place where sinners go after death)
parole.testo: From Ottoman Turkish طامو (tamu), from Old Anatolian Turkish طامو (tamu), from Proto-Common Turkic *tamu (“hell”), ultimately from Sogdian. Cognate with Tatar тәмуг (tämuğ, “hell”), Uzbek tamugʻ (“hell”), Uyghur تامۇق (tamuq, “hell”), Bashkir тамуҡ (tamuq, “hell”).
